title: Aspirin use and colorectal cancer risk: a cohort study.
abstract: Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer death worldwide.
We followed 82,000 adults for 20 years to assess regular aspirin use.
Regular aspirin use was associated with a significantly reduced risk of colorectal cancer (HR 0.77).
The protective association was strongest after more than 10 years of use.
Aspirin use did not affect the risk of lung cancer.

title: Vitamin D supplementation and fracture prevention in older adults.
abstract: Fractures cause substantial morbidity in older adults.
We randomized 25,000 participants aged over 70 to vitamin D or placebo.
Vitamin D supplementation did not reduce the incidence of fractures compared with placebo.
Falls were similar in both groups.
These results do not support routine vitamin D supplementation for fracture prevention.

title: Exercise training improves insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Insulin resistance is central to type 2 diabetes.
Patients were assigned to 12 weeks of aerobic exercise or usual care.
Exercise training increased insulin sensitivity by 25% relative to control.
HbA1c decreased significantly in the exercise group.
Body weight changed little.

title: Smoking and the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a major cause of disability.
We analysed 15,000 smokers and never-smokers.
Current smoking increased the risk of COPD fourfold.
Smoking cessation slowed the decline in lung function.

title: Gut microbiota composition in obesity.
abstract: The gut microbiome influences host energy balance.
We sequenced stool samples from 300 lean and obese individuals.
Obese individuals had lower microbial diversity than lean individuals.
The ratio of Firmicutes to Bacteroidetes was higher in obesity.

title: Statin therapy and cardiovascular events in primary prevention.
abstract: Statins lower LDL cholesterol.
In this trial 17,802 adults without cardiovascular disease received rosuvastatin or placebo.
Rosuvastatin reduced major cardiovascular events by 44%.
Rates of myocardial infarction and stroke were significantly lower with statin therapy.

title: Sleep deprivation impairs memory consolidation.
abstract: Sleep supports the consolidation of new memories.
Volunteers were deprived of sleep for one night after learning word pairs.
Sleep deprivation impaired recall of word pairs by 40% compared with normal sleep.
Hippocampal activity during retrieval was reduced after sleep loss.

title: Coffee consumption and the risk of Parkinson disease.
abstract: Parkinson disease is a neurodegenerative disorder.
We examined coffee intake among 300,000 adults.
Higher coffee consumption was associated with a lower risk of Parkinson disease.
The association was not observed for decaffeinated coffee.

title: Antibiotic exposure in infancy and childhood asthma.
abstract: Asthma is the most common chronic disease in children.
We studied 50,000 children and their antibiotic prescriptions before age one.
Early antibiotic exposure was associated with an increased risk of asthma.
The risk increased with the number of antibiotic courses.

title: Mediterranean diet and cognitive decline.
abstract: Diet may influence brain ageing.
We followed 2,000 elderly adults for six years.
Adherence to a Mediterranean diet was associated with slower cognitive decline.
No association was found with incident stroke.
